topic.title: CSS — Quick Revision
topic.subtitle: Layout, specificity and the box model — the CSS interview core.

answer.value: Every element is a box: **content → padding → border → margin**. With `box-sizing: content-box` (default) `width` covers only the content; with `border-box` it includes padding and border, which is why most resets use `* { box-sizing: border-box }`.
Compare in order: inline style > IDs > classes/attributes/pseudo-classes > elements/pseudo-elements. `!important` overrides normal rules. With equal specificity the later rule wins.

questions.q: Flexbox: main axis vs cross axis, and the key properties?

items: `display:flex` on the container; `flex-direction` sets the main axis.
`justify-content` aligns along the main axis; `align-items` along the cross axis.

questions.q: Flexbox vs Grid — when do you use each?

answer.value: Flexbox is **one-dimensional** (a row or a column) — ideal for toolbars, nav and centring. Grid is **two-dimensional** (rows and columns together) — ideal for page layouts and card galleries.

questions.q: How do you centre a div horizontally and vertically?
position: static, relative, absolute, fixed, sticky?

items: **relative**: offset from its normal spot; creates a positioning context.
**absolute**: removed from flow, positioned against the nearest positioned ancestor.
**sticky**: relative until a scroll threshold, then fixed.

questions.q: What is the difference between em, rem, %, vh/vw?

items: `rem` — relative to the root font size (predictable scaling).
`em` — relative to the element's (or parent's) font size; compounds when nested.
`%` — relative to the parent's corresponding property.

questions.q: How do you build a responsive layout?

answer.value: Start mobile-first with fluid units, flexible grids and `max-width`. Add `@media (min-width: …)` breakpoints, use `clamp()` for fluid type, and `<meta name="viewport">`. Container queries let a component respond to its own container instead of the viewport.

questions.q: What is a stacking context and how does z-index work?

answer.value: `z-index` only orders elements within the same stacking context. A new context is created by the root, positioned elements with a z-index, `opacity < 1`, `transform`, `filter`, `isolation: isolate` and more. A child can never escape its parent's context.

questions.q: display: none vs visibility: hidden vs opacity: 0?

items: `display:none` — removed from layout and accessibility tree.
`opacity:0` — invisible, occupies space and still receives events.

answer.value: Defined with `--name` and read with `var(--name, fallback)`. They cascade and inherit, can change at runtime with JS, and make theming (e.g. dark mode) simple.
Pseudo-classes select an element in a state (`:hover`, `:focus-visible`, `:nth-child()`, `:not()`). Pseudo-elements style a part of it or generate content (`::before`, `::after`, `::placeholder`).

Adjacent vertical margins of block elements (siblings, or parent and first/last child) combine into one — the larger wins. It doesn't happen in flex or grid containers, or when padding/border separates the margins.

questions.q: How do transitions and animations differ?

answer.value: A **transition** animates between two states when a property changes. A **@keyframes animation** can run on load, have many steps, loop and be controlled independently. Prefer animating `transform` and `opacity` for smooth, GPU-friendly results.
`clamp(min, preferred, max)` picks a value that grows with the viewport but is bounded, e.g. `font-size: clamp(1rem, 2vw + .5rem, 2rem)` — fluid typography without media queries.
